q: Which country's flag features a single red maple leaf?
note: The maple leaf flag was adopted in 1965, replacing a design based on the British Red Ensign.

q: Which country flies a flag showing a plain red circle on a white field?
note: The Japanese call it the Hinomaru, meaning circle of the sun.

q: How many time zones does the contiguous United States span?
note: Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific, with Alaska and Hawaii adding two more beyond them.

q: What is the name of the imaginary line at zero degrees latitude?
note: It crosses through Ecuador, Kenya, Indonesia and Brazil, among other countries.

q: What is the name of the line of zero degrees longitude that runs through Greenwich, England?
note: An international conference fixed it at Greenwich in 1884, beating out rival lines through Paris and elsewhere.

q: What is the name of the line running roughly down the middle of the Pacific where the calendar date changes?
note: It zigzags rather than running straight, so island groups can keep the same day as their neighbors.

q: Which is the only country whose national flag is not a rectangle or a square?
note: Nepal's flag is two stacked triangular pennants, a shape carried over from much older banners.

q: Which country flies a square flag bearing a white cross on red?
note: Switzerland and Vatican City are the only two countries whose flags are square.

q: Which South American country borders more other countries than any other on the continent?
note: Brazil touches every country in South America except Chile and Ecuador.

q: What is the name of the line of latitude marking the northern edge of the tropics?
note: It marks the farthest north the sun can ever stand directly overhead, which happens around June 21.

q: Which country lies south of North Korea, across a border first drawn along the 38th parallel?
note: The two were split along that line in 1945, and the demilitarized zone still runs near it.

q: Which country's flag shows a blue Star of David between two blue horizontal stripes?
note: The stripes echo the bands on a traditional Jewish prayer shawl.

q: What is the name of the narrow strip of land that joins North and South America?
note: The Panama Canal cuts straight through it, saving ships the long trip around South America.

q: Which continent has no permanent human residents?
note: Antarctica also counts as the world's largest desert, since almost no precipitation falls there.

q: Besides Vatican City, which other tiny republic is entirely surrounded by Italy?
note: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic, traditionally dated to AD 301.

q: Which Himalayan kingdom flies a flag featuring a white dragon?
note: Bhutan calls itself Druk Yul, which means Land of the Thunder Dragon.

q: Which African country is surrounded by Senegal on every side except its short Atlantic coast?
note: The country is essentially a narrow ribbon of land following the banks of the river it is named for.

q: Which US state contains the Northwest Angle, the only part of the lower 48 states lying north of the 49th parallel?
note: The Angle is cut off from the rest of the state by water, so driving there means passing through Canada.

q: Which is the only US state whose name begins with two vowels?
note: Ohio, Oregon, Oklahoma and Utah all start with a vowel, but each follows it with a consonant.

q: Which Pacific island nation lies in all four hemispheres at once?
note: Its islands straddle both the equator and the 180th meridian, and in 1995 it shifted the date line east so the whole country shares one day.
